candidate.blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — apixaban dose-reduction criteria
candidate.educational_objective: Apply the labeled apixaban NVAF dose-reduction rule: 2.5 mg twice daily when at least two of the three specified age, weight, and serum-creatinine criteria are present.

options.A: Reduce to 2.5 mg twice daily when at least two of these criteria are present: age 80 years or older, body weight 60 kg or less, or serum creatinine 1.5 mg/dL or greater.
options.B: Reduce to 2.5 mg twice daily whenever any degree of renal impairment is documented, regardless of age or body weight.
options.C: Keep the dose unchanged because age, body weight, and serum creatinine do not affect labeled NVAF dosing.
options.D: Increase the dose whenever serum creatinine reaches 1.5 mg/dL because lower renal clearance requires more drug to maintain effect.

candidate.rationale: Current ELIQUIS labeling recommends 5 mg twice daily for most adults with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation and 2.5 mg twice daily when at least two of three criteria are present: age 80 years or older, body weight 60 kg or less, or serum creatinine 1.5 mg/dL or greater. A is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: For adult NVAF, apixaban dose reduction to 2.5 mg twice daily is based on the presence of at least two of the three labeled age, body-weight, and serum-creatinine criteria.
candidate.source_locator: §2.1 Recommended Dose in Adult Patients: NVAF usual dose 5 mg twice daily; reduce to 2.5 mg twice daily when at least two of age ≥80 years, body weight ≤60 kg, or serum creatinine ≥1.5 mg/dL are present.
candidate.source_organization: DailyMed / U.S. National Library of Medicine official drug label
candidate.stem: A client with nonvalvular atrial fibrillation is prescribed apixaban. Which statement about the labeled adult dose-reduction criteria is accurate?
